apparatus.basis: Standard Coptic ⲛ̄ⲥⲏⲩ ⲛⲓⲙ 'at every season,' paired with ⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ ⲛⲓⲙ 'every hour' on the next line.
Standard interjection ⲉⲓⲥ 'behold,' opening the introduction of the second mystery; only ⲥ visible at line start.
ⲛⲁⲙⲉⲣⲉⲧⲉ 'my beloved (pl.)' — single character ⲉ restored to complete the address; continues into next line.
ⲛⲉⲧⲟⲩⲉⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'those that come forth' — the verbal phrase ⲉⲓ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ continues onto next line where ⲁⲃⲁⲗ is preserved.
Continues across line break; only -ⲓ̈ⲛⲉ visible. The phrase ⲡⲙⲩⲥⲧⲏⲣⲓⲟⲛ ⲙ̄ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ ⲙⲛ̄ ⲡⲙⲩⲥⲧⲏⲣⲓⲟⲛ ⲙ̄ⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ 'the mystery of the light and the mystery of the darkness' is the standard Manichaean dyad.

notes.decision: Translated 'the third' (feminine ordinal). The doubled ⲧⲧ- represents article + ordinal-prefix. The implied feminine antecedent (saying / sign / mystery) is ambiguous; left bare 'the third' to preserve the enumerative force without unwarranted specification.

Rendered 'raised' preserving the verbal-directional sense of ⲧⲟⲩⲱ (per terminology guide). Here functioning as verbal noun parallel to qualitative ⲭⲁⲥⲉ 'is exalted/high' — a doublet of elevation-vocabulary. Vertical semantics retained, not flattened.

Rendered 'is hidden.' The element ⲙⲁⲍⲁⲓ̈ⲡⲉ likely relates to ⲡⲙⲁⲍⲁⲓ̈ⲡⲧⲉ 'hidden chamber/repository' (accumulated vocabulary), here functioning verbally with subject prefix ϥ̄- 'he.' Possible analysis: ⲙⲁ-ⲍⲁⲓ̈ⲡⲉ ('place-of-hiding') with predicative use, yielding 'he is in (a) hidden state.' Same root as ⲍⲏⲡ 'hidden' (line 21, 26).

Rendered 'of heaven. As visions, behold them...' — parsing ⲙ̄ⲡⲉ as 'of heaven' (Sah. ⲡⲉ 'heaven, sky') governed by ⲡⲥⲱⲱⲛⲧ̄ 'creation,' giving 'creation of heaven.' ⲛ̄ⲁⲟⲣⲙⲁ then begins a new clause: '(as) visions, behold them in their wandering.' Alternative reading 'the two visions' (treating ⲙ̄ⲡⲉ as scribal abbreviation for ⲡⲓⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲉⲩ) is possible but less natural.

Greek loanwords ἄταφος 'unburied' in three forms: indefinite (ⲟⲩⲁⲧⲁⲫⲟⲥ), definite neuter (ⲡⲁⲧⲁⲫⲟⲛ), and adjectival (ⲛⲁⲧⲁⲫⲟⲥ). The cosmological doctrine: the Sun is 'unburied' — i.e., not subjected to dissolution/decay, sharing this quality of substance with the unburied Father. Direct correspondence between Sun and Father preserved in the three-fold repetition.

Translated 'shadow.' Feminine form of ϩⲁⲓⲃⲉⲥ 'shadow' (cf. ⲍⲁⲃⲉⲥ in glossary, masculine form). Lycopolitan ⲍ for ϩ. The night-as-shadow stands in correspondence with the cosmic darkness-mystery, paralleling sun-as-light corresponding to Father-mystery.
ⲛⲟⲩⲭⲉ = ⲛⲟⲩϫⲉ 'cast, throw' + ⲛⲟⲩⲭⲱⲣⲙⲉ from ϫⲱⲣⲙ 'wink, signal.' Idiom: 'cast a sign, give a winking signal.' The Savior gives a hidden indication to the disciples about the hidden mystery.

Read as functioning negation marker ('not'), yielding 'You are NOT sons of the night and sons of the darkness.' This matches the Pauline source (1 Thess 5:5) which the apostle is quoting. ⲛ̄ⲧⲁϩ may be a Lycopolitan variant or scribal form of the negative ⲁⲛ; alternative parsings (relative perfect 'who became,' or as connective 'of those of') do not yield the expected biblical sense. The doctrinal context (children of light vs. darkness) and the ⲡⲁⲭⲉ ⲡⲁⲡⲟⲥⲧⲟⲗⲟⲥ 'said the apostle' framing make the Pauline citation certain.
